phase: R5.5 Phase 16 - Collapse root-cause decision tree
data_origin: local CPU diagnostics (r5_5_local_baselines.py) + Kaggle GPU kernels v7 (image+tabular, 2 epochs) and v8 (Phase-11 tiny-overfit) + earlier R5.5/R5.2.9/R5.3 phase reports

Q1_is_label_pipeline_correct.evidence: R5.5_label_trace.json: label_mapping_ok=true, split_counts_match_manifest=true, gate_equals_trivial_coconut_anchor=true; declared class order coconut=0,pepper=1,coffee=2,cardamom=3 matches head+evaluator
Q1_is_label_pipeline_correct.impact: collapse is NOT a label-ordering bug

Q2_is_imbalance_extreme.evidence: train counts coconut=4292 (72.4%), pepper=1599 (27.0%), coffee=29 (0.49%), cardamom=4 (0.068%); majority prior val acc=0.5584 / test=0.5242
Q2_is_imbalance_extreme.impact: extreme imbalance is an intrinsic ceiling for ALL models

Q3_do_tabular_features_separate_classes.evidence: R5.5_local_baselines.json tabular section: every model on the frozen official split fails to beat the majority predictor. Best mispredictor = gb_numeric (acc 0.5392, coffee 30/21) but macro_f1 0.26 with coffee precision ~0.02. lr balanced predicts 620 coffee for 21 real (precision 0.0113). Binary coconut-vs-pepper: best LR AUC=0.5524 (nearly random).
Q3_do_tabular_features_separate_classes.answer: NO (tabular features offer almost no inter-class signal)
Q3_do_tabular_features_separate_classes.impact: the collapse IS present even for simple tabular models - not a complexity bug

Q4_are_classes_spatially_colocated_or_se.evidence: R5.5_phase6_spatial_audit.json village_colocation_train: pepper shares 118/118 villages with coconut, coffee 17/17, cardamom 4/4; all samples live in the same taluk grid cells (env_match_distance median 148m). R5.5_local_baselines.json duplicates: 94% of train within 500m of a neighbor, pepper median NN=54.7m coffee=69.9m cardamom=80.3m. Centroid distances: coconut-vs-pepper only 5.7km.
Q4_are_classes_spatially_colocated_or_se.impact: spatial co-location means satellite/env features are largely identical across classes

Q5_is_the_loss/weights_arithmetic_correc.evidence: R5.5_local_baselines.json loss_audit: sqrt_inv weights and balanced weights are gathered along the TARGET dim (correct); ratios match training config. focal_gamma=2.0 suppresses the target-token grad by (1-p)^2; sqrt_inv x coffee=12.17x coefficient is largely cancelled by focal suppression. Per-sample grad norms: focal_g2_sqrt_inv gives coffee=0.2395 vs coconut=0.3285 (coffee < coconut!) though cardamom=0.408 is biggest.
Q5_is_the_loss/weights_arithmetic_correc.answer: YES (arithmetic correct) BUT the deployed loss is suboptimal for ultra-rare classes
Q5_is_the_loss/weights_arithmetic_correc.impact: gradient mechanics confirmed; focal+sqrt_inv+label-smoothing jointly dilute the rare-class signal

Q6_does_the_model_train_at_all.evidence: R3 default model trained, acc=0.5636 on val (== majority prior, predicts all-coconut). Kaggle GPU v7: scheduler fixed (80bc3263); Phase 3 binary ran cleanly 2 epochs - loss descends (train 0.1147 -> 0.1122 default), no NaN, val acc 0.5636 == prior. Phase 10 first-step dynamics: train_loss 0.0776 -> 0.0545, probe acc 0.5 -> 0.61, coconut-pepper logit gap positive. Kaggle GPU v8 Phase 11: a balanced 40-sample (20+20) tiny set is memorized to probe acc 1.0 by step 29 of 300, train_loss -> 0.0001.
Q6_does_the_model_train_at_all.answer: YES - model trains healthily on GPU and has ample capacity (memorizes a balanced 40-sample set to 100%); it never escapes coconut collapse on the full corpus
Q6_does_the_model_train_at_all.impact: the NN is NOT underfitting or capacity-limited; the collapse on the full corpus is caused by the data distribution, not the model

Q7_do_image_features_differ.evidence: Kaggle GPU Phase 5/9 (fitted preprocessor, train subset): per-class NDVI mean 0.611 (coconut) / 0.616 (pepper) / 0.643 (coffee) / 0.617 (cardamom); EVI mean 0.662/0.663/0.668/0.645 - near-identical. zero_fill_frac 0.539-0.656 (53-66% of 8 temporal frames are padding, mask mean 0.396 in first batch). Phase 3 binary with imagery: default collapses all-coconut ([[1373,0],[1063,0]]); balanced CE pepper prec 0.353/recall 0.136 below majority.
Q7_do_image_features_differ.answer: NO - real-frame statistics are near-identical across classes and the temporal stack is mostly zero-fill padding; image+tabular training does not separate classes
Q7_do_image_features_differ.impact: image separability question is now RESOLVED for the statistics + joint-binary level; a strict image-ONLY training curve (Phase 15) is the only remaining niche

Q8_does_simple_ensemble_or_threshold_hel.evidence: R5.5_phase4_sweep (variants held on val): focal+sqrt_inv gave val acc 0.5584 macro-F1 0.1791 EXACTLY the majority anchor. No loss variant beat it. Newer sweep set to hold on test.
Q8_does_simple_ensemble_or_threshold_hel.impact: loss re-weighting ALONE cannot fix it - data ceiling is the binding constraint

traced_failure_chain: 1) extreme class imbalance (4292/4 coconut-to-cardamom) sets a 0.5584 prior ceiling
2) classes are spatially co-located (all taluk grid cells shared, 94% within 500m) so env + satellite features are near-identical between classes
3) tabular features alone cannot distinguish classes (LR/RF/GB/MLP all <= majority; binary LR AUC=0.55)
4) the loss re-weighting (focal+sqrt_inv+0.15 smoothing) is arithmetic-sound but cancels the rare-class boost at uncertain draws
5) the only truly informative feature is geographic (lat/lon) - a leak-adjacent split shortcut

6) GPU image+tabular run (kernel v7): default binary still collapses to all-coconut (confusion [[1373,0],[1063,0]]), balanced CE hits only 0.353 pepper precision, per-class NDVI/EVI stats near-identical and 53-66% of temporal frames are zero-fill -> image modality does not unlock separation
primary_root_cause: CEILING: the frozen corpus is fundamentally spatially co-located and dominated by coconut; NO tabular model can beat the majority predictor, and loss re-weighting cannot manufacture signal that does not exist in the data - GPU-verified for the image modality too
secondary_root_cause: RARE-CLASS DILUTION: coffee=29 / cardamom=4 train samples sit inside coconut-heavy village pixels; focal(gamma=2)+label-smoothing(0.15) further suppress the already-weak rare-class gradient
open_question: RESOLVED at statistics + joint-binary + capacity levels (Kaggle GPU v7+v8). The only residual niche is a strict image-ONLY training curve (Phase 15 modality ablation), which is not expected to change the verdict given Phase 3's joint collapse at exactly the majority prior.
recommended_next_change: Do NOT loosen matching rules or add imagery blindly (imagery already shown non-separating on GPU; model capacity shown sufficient in Phase 11). Next: small locked test-eval experiment where cardamom/coffee are EXCLUDED from training loss but scored independently on leftovers; and/or a per-pixel patch-level binary 'interior-vs-monoculture' probe. Validate on the frozen split.
success_criteria_confidence_notes: CONFIDENT about data-ceiling (tabular + spatial + GPU image evidence is decisive)
CONFIDENT about loss arithmetic being correct but suboptimal for ultra-rare
GPU phases 3/5/9/10 (v7) and phase 11 (v8) VERIFIED completed; phase 15 (image-only) not run
